1-based row index of the multilocus simulation inside its batch files. Rows are paired by position across ABCstat.txt, ABCjsfs.txt and priorfile.txt.
Strict isolation: an ancestral population splits at Tsplit and the daughter populations never exchange genes afterwards.

Ancestral migration: the daughter populations exchange genes after the split, then isolation begins at Tam. There is no ongoing migration, so AM belongs to the isolation class, but 1M/2M still describe ancient migration.
Isolation with migration: the daughter populations exchange genes continuously from the split until the present.
Secondary contact: the daughter populations first evolve in isolation, then resume gene exchange at Tsc.
Homogeneous genomic migration: all loci share the same migration rate in a given direction.

Heterogeneous genomic migration under the bimodal barrier model: loci belong to two classes, one migrating at the general rate and one barrier class whose migration rate is zero. Barrier loci can differ between M12 and M21.
Homogeneous Ne: all loci share the same effective population size.
Heterogeneous Ne: effective size varies among genomic regions, which can capture linked-selection effects that reduce Ne locally.
